plain_claim: For every program, encoding parameters and start assignment a, the grow-only relaxation loop (each pass promotes, simultaneously, every short branch that is out of reach in the current layout; the loop stops when a pass would change nothing) stops within numBranches + 1 passes and returns exactly relax prm p a, the numBranches-fold iterate of the grow-only step; no hypothesis on sizes or alignment is needed.
nonvacuity_witness: Two-branch promotion chain [fixed 2, branch 0, branch 1], short 1/long 2/reach 1: all-short is invalid and the returned assignment has both branches long.
non_claims: Does not say the result is least or of minimum total size; leastness needs monotone distances (R1c) and minimum size needs monotone distances and shortSize <= longSize (R4a).

The bound counts all branches and is attained (relaxLoop_numBranches_passes_insufficient). A sharper bound (the number of short branch positions in the start, plus one) is stated separately as the auxiliary lemma Toy.Relax.relaxLoop_spec.

Grow-only termination does not extend to grow-and-shrink relaxation (each branch i re-decided from the counterfactual layout setShort a i, long branches may be demoted), which can oscillate forever (from a non-bottom start with monotone sizes, R3a; from all-short without monotone distances, R3c).

Simultaneous (Jacobi) updates only. A sequential pass that re-lays out the program after each promotion is not part of the model; a support check (Search/Sequential.lean, kernel-checked by decide, not a library result) shows that on [branch 3, branch 3, align 4] with short 1, long 2, reach 2 it stops at a different valid assignment (only branch 0 long) than the simultaneous passes (branches 0 and 1 long).

Two encodings per branch with unbounded long reach only: instruction sets with more than two branch sizes (where more passes can be needed) and long forms with a finite reach (where relaxation can fail) are not modeled.

No convergence or validity claim is made about LLVM's MCAssembler::relaxOnce, which updates offsets in place during a pass, also relaxes non-branch fragments (LEB128 values, CFI advance deltas, alignment), and stops a section after a pass count derived from its fragment count.

Toy model only: the results apply to the Lean model Toy.Relax (two encodings per branch, instruction-index targets, simultaneous updates); no property of a real assembler or linker is established by the Lean proofs, and every connection to a real toolchain is a separately labeled derived modeling bridge.

hypotheses.purpose: a branch that is out of reach under a stays out of reach under any b above a, so every promotion is forced

hypotheses.purpose: relaxation never demotes, so it cannot go below its start

plain_claim: The distance between the start of the instruction at i and the start of the instruction at t depends only on the sizes of the instructions in [min i t, max i t), and is monotone in them: if each of those sizes under a is at most its size under b, the distance under a is at most the distance under b.

Indices >= p.length are clamped: the address of any such index is the end address of the program, so the distance to a target t >= p.length is the distance to the end.

plain_claim: Grow-and-shrink relaxation, in which each branch i is re-decided from the counterfactual layout setShort a i (branch i tentatively short, every other position as in a) and long branches may be demoted, can oscillate forever even with monotone sizes when started from a non-bottom assignment: on [fixed 1, branch 3, branch 0] (short 1, long 2, reach 2), started from 'branch 1 long', it alternates forever between 'branch 1 long, branch 2 short' and 'branch 1 short, branch 2 long'.
nonvacuity_witness: The instance itself; on it grow-only relaxation from the same start converges and grow-and-shrink from all-short is already at a fixpoint.
non_claims: The oscillation uses a start that is not all-short; from all-short and under monotone distances grow-and-shrink cannot oscillate (R3b), while without monotone distances it can oscillate from all-short as well (R3c).

The counterfactual reading matters: reading branch i's distance from the current layout a instead differs on forward long branches, whose own size lies in their span; from the start of this instance, branch 1 is out of short reach in the current layout but fits when tentatively short (stepGS_decides_from_counterfactual_layout). The contrast definition stepGSCurrent, which reads the current layout, does not oscillate on this instance: from the same start it makes both branches long, a valid fixpoint (osc_stepGSCurrent_reaches_valid_fixpoint). No general result about stepGSCurrent is stated.

Two branches is the minimum number for any oscillation: with one branch, setShort a i makes the layout independent of a, so its decision is constant after one step - derived argument, not formalized; minimality in instruction count is not claimed.

plain_claim: Let a be a valid assignment, promote any position j to long and re-run grow-only relaxation, obtaining r = relax prm p (promote a j). If every instruction inside the program has positive size in layout a and in layout r, then for every branch i with target t, in each of the two layouts the branch has an encodable displacement (emitDisp: the branch is long, or short and within reach) and that displacement, recomputed from its own layout, lands on an instruction index k <= p.length exactly when k = min t p.length; in particular the two displacements land on the same instruction indices.

hypotheses.purpose: distinct instruction indices have distinct addresses in layout a

hypotheses.purpose: distinct instruction indices have distinct addresses in layout r; promotion can shrink alignment padding to 0 bytes

plain_claim: If the abstract interpretation (tracking the sp delta, register contents and stack-slot contents symbolically) assigns no caller-visible register the rule undefined at any offset, then the table it generates is correct: at every offset it recovers the caller's sp (CFA) and the entry values of all caller-visible registers, for every entry state.

Single-frame virtual unwinding only: TableCorrect does not forbid the body from writing into the caller's frame (addresses >= entry sp; tableCorrect_permits_caller_frame_write) and does not require the body to restore sp or any register by its end (tableCorrect_permits_unrestored_sp).
